tldr: MEM1 is an end-to-end reinforcement learning framework that enables LLM agents to maintain constant memory across arbitrarily long multi-turn tasks by learning to consolidate prior memory and new observations into a compact internal state at each turn.
contributions: MEM1: an end-to-end RL framework where agents learn reasoning-driven memory consolidation, maintaining near-constant memory usage by updating a shared internal state and discarding irrelevant/redundant information each turn
A masked trajectory approach with 2D attention masking for policy optimization under dynamically updated contexts
A scalable multi-objective task augmentation method that composes existing single-objective QA datasets into arbitrarily complex multi-hop task sequences
Demonstration across three domains (internal retrieval QA, open-domain web QA, multi-turn web shopping) showing significant efficiency and performance gains
methods: MEM1 trains agents end-to-end with PPO reinforcement learning, where at each turn the model generates an internal state <IS> that consolidates prior memory with new environment observations, then produces a query or answer action. After each turn, all previous context tags are pruned except the prompt, initial query, and the most recent <IS>, <query>, and <info> elements, keeping context bounded. A two-dimensional attention mask is applied during policy updates to correctly compute token-wise advantages despite the dynamic context. The authors also construct multi-objective QA tasks by interleaving multiple questions from existing datasets (HotpotQA, Natural Questions) into composite queries requiring N search-and-reasoning turns.
results: MEM1-7B improves performance by 3.5× while reducing memory usage by 3.7× compared to Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct on a 16-objective multi-hop QA task. At the 16-objective level, MEM1 achieves superior accuracy versus all baselines, with 1.27× lower peak memory usage and 1.78× faster inference compared to the best uncollapsed baseline. The agent trained on 2-objective compositions generalizes effectively to up to 16-objective tasks. Improvements were demonstrated across internal retrieval QA, open-domain web QA, and multi-turn web shopping (WebShop).
limitations: Existing benchmarks like HotpotQA, Bamboogle, and 2wiki typically involve only two information-seeking steps and are not explicitly structured for long-horizon memory management
Limited publicly available datasets support training for long-horizon interactive processes
The task augmentation composes existing single-objective datasets, which may not fully capture the complexity of all real-world scenarios
